NexusFlow SaaS Billing & Usage Reconciliation Notice
To: Marcus Thorne, CFO, Veridian Dynamics
From: Elena Rostova, Billing Operations, NexusFlow Inc.
Date: 14 November 2024
Reference: INV-2024-11-8842 / Usage Cycle: 01 Oct – 31 Oct 2024

This notice reconciles your October usage against your Enterprise Tier contract (Ref: ENT-VD-2023, Account ID: ACC-VD-7742). The contract baseline threshold is 100 seats. Standard billing applies at $45 per active seat per month. Usage data indicates 112 seats were active on 15 October, triggering the threshold.

Adjustment Policy (Section 4.2):
(a) Overage applies if active seats exceed the contracted baseline on the mid-cycle measurement date (the 15th of the billing month).
(b) "Active seat" is defined strictly as a user account with a successful API authentication or dashboard login within the measurement window; dormant accounts, test environments, and service accounts are excluded.
(c) Adjustments are calculated on a pro-rata basis for the remaining days of the cycle, excluding the measurement date itself.
(d) If a seat is deactivated within 48 hours of the measurement date, it is retroactively removed from the overage calculation, provided the deactivation log timestamp is verified by NexusFlow security systems.
(e) All billed amounts are subject to the applicable regional VAT, which is calculated on the pre-adjustment subtotal and added post-calculation.

Your October baseline is 100 seats. Measured active seats: 112. Overage: 12 seats.
Days remaining after 15 Oct: 16.
Overage calculation: 12 seats × $67.50 × (16/31) = $417.55.
VAT (20%): $83.51.
Total adjustment due: $501.06.

Note on Seat #112 (User: j.kim@veridian.dev): This account logged in on 15 Oct at 09:14 UTC but was deactivated on 16 Oct at 14:30 UTC. The deactivation falls within the 48-hour window. However, our security audit log (ID: SEC-LOG-9921) shows the deactivation request originated from an unverified external IP range, failing the verification requirement in clause (d). Therefore, Seat #112 remains in the overage calculation.

Payment is due by 30 November 2024. Please remit to the account on file or reply to schedule a payment plan. This statement replaces preliminary estimates. Discrepancies must be reported within five business days. NexusFlow reserves audit rights for quarterly compliance verification.

NEXUSFLOW ANALYTICS | ENTERPRISE ESCALATION DOSSIER #NF-8842
CLIENT: Veridian Logistics Inc.
ACCOUNT TIER: Platinum (Contract v4.2)
INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION: Data Pipeline Latency Spike
CASE OWNER: Elena Rostova, Senior Support Architect
DATE FILED: 2024-03-14
PRIORITY DIRECTIVE: Minimize immediate cash outflow while ensuring long-term account retention.

CHRONOLOGICAL EVENT LOG
2024-03-10 14:30 UTC: Veridian internal DevOps deploys middleware patch v2.1.4 to staging cluster without prior NexusFlow compatibility review.
2024-03-14 02:14 UTC: NexusFlow monitoring detects ETL job completion delays averaging 2,800ms response time across four primary ingestion nodes.
2024-03-14 02:18 UTC: Client logs initial ticket #TK-9921 reporting dashboard staleness and intermittent timeout warnings.
2024-03-14 06:00 UTC: Tier-2 support escalates to Tier-3 Engineering due to volume of impacted endpoints and client SLA threshold breach warnings.
2024-03-14 08:45 UTC: Latency resolves after auto-scaling triggers and temporary quota expansion. Total impact duration: 6 hours 31 minutes.
2024-03-14 09:10 UTC: Root cause analysis confirms throttled API quota on staging cluster, compounded by unpatched middleware v2.1.4 deployed by client. No data loss. Core API endpoint remained fully available throughout.

APPLICABLE ESCALATION POLICY (SECTION 7.C)
DEFINITION: "Service Disruption" refers strictly to backend infrastructure failure causing complete unavailability of the core API endpoint for a continuous period exceeding fifteen minutes. This definition explicitly excludes client-side misconfigurations, third-party dependency timeouts, and performance degradation where response times remain under 4,500ms.
CLAUSE 1: If a Service Disruption occurs during a Platinum tier account’s business hours (08:00-18:00 client local time), the Tier-3 Engineering squad must engage within forty-five minutes of ticket creation.
CLAUSE 2: Performance degradation incidents classified as "Non-Critical Latency" (sustained response times between 1,500ms and 4,500ms) trigger a Standard Diagnostic Workflow, requiring engineer engagement within four hours of ticket creation.
CLAUSE 3: Any incident involving a client-deployed unpatched middleware version (as cataloged in Appendix B) automatically voids Clause 1 SLA guarantees and shifts liability for diagnostic costs to the client, per Section 9.1.
CLAUSE 4: Service credits are only eligible if the root cause is exclusively attributable to NexusFlow infrastructure and the incident duration exceeds sixty minutes.
CLAUSE 5: If a client opts for a proactive architecture audit to prevent recurrence, audit fees are waived provided the incident occurred within the first ninety days of a contract renewal cycle.

RESOLUTION PATHWAYS & FINANCIAL IMPLICATIONS
PATHWAY A: Issue a standard percentage-based service credit. Cost: Calculated at trailing 90-day average invoice value. Constraint: Requires exclusive NexusFlow liability per Clause 4.
PATHWAY B: Deploy a dedicated rate-limit bypass for the staging cluster. Cost: Zero immediate cash outflow; requires a 15% price adjustment on the next renewal invoice. Constraint: Available exclusively for Gold tier accounts or higher.
PATHWAY C: Schedule a complimentary enterprise architecture audit. Cost: Waived professional services fee (retail valuation $12,000). Constraint: Requires incident to fall within the 90-day renewal window AND client executive sign-off on a mandatory 12-month contract extension.
PATHWAY D: Issue a full incident refund for affected operational days. Cost: Pro-rated daily subscription fee. Constraint: Permitted only if a formal Service Disruption classification is achieved.

REFERENCE MATRIX: SLA & CREDIT CAPS (POLICY VERSIONS)
Version 3.1 (Superseded 2022-06-01): Platinum Latency Credit Cap: 15% | Tier-3 Response SLA: 2 hours
Version 4.0 (Superseded 2023-01-15): Platinum Latency Credit Cap: 12% | Tier-3 Response SLA: 1.5 hours
Version 4.1 (Active until 2024-01-01): Platinum Latency Credit Cap: 10% | Tier-3 Response SLA: 1 hour
Version 4.2 (Current, effective 2024-01-02): Platinum Latency Credit Cap: 10% | Tier-3 Response SLA: 45 minutes (Service Disruption) / 4 hours (Non-Critical Latency)
Note: All financial thresholds apply to the current active version. Superseded values are retained for historical audit trails only. Credit calculations utilize the trailing 90-day average invoice value, excluding one-time setup fees.

COMPLIANCE & PENDING FIELDS
Current Status: Awaiting client selection between Pathway B and Pathway C.
Pending Verification: Exact UTC deployment timestamp and approval signature for Veridian’s middleware v2.1.4 rollout. This artifact is mandatory to finalize liability assignment under Clause 3.
Contract Renewal Date: 2024-03-25.

Next Review: 2024-03-18 10:00 UTC.

INCIDENT REPORT & COMPLIANCE PROTOCOL REFERENCE
Case ID: NXF-8842
Date: 2024-10-15
Parties: Aethelgard Logistics (Client) / NexusFlow Analytics (Vendor)
Subject: Data Pipeline Latency & Service Interruption

1. INCIDENT SUMMARY & METADATA
On 2024-10-15 at 14:30 UTC, NexusFlow’s primary analytics dashboard experienced intermittent latency, escalating to a full service interruption at 15:05 UTC. Service was fully restored at 19:40 UTC. The incident impacted 612 concurrent daily active users processing real-time shipment tracking data. Financial transaction processing was not directly affected, as billing modules run on isolated legacy servers. The interruption originated from an automated failover routine triggered by a memory leak in the secondary cache cluster. Data integrity checks confirm zero record loss. Incident metadata tags include: [Priority: High, Region: EU-West, Compliance_Flag: PII_Processing, Audit_Trail: Pending_Compliance_Check]. Estimated client financial exposure: $38,500. Maintenance notice for the cache cluster was dispatched exactly 72 hours prior to the outage window. Historical resolution confidence score for this incident pattern: 89%.

2. DEFINITIONS & CLASSIFICATION FRAMEWORK
Clause 2.1 (Tier Classification): Service Tiers are assigned based on user volume and system function. A “Critical System” is strictly defined as any production-facing application serving more than 500 concurrent daily active users AND performing direct financial transaction processing. Systems failing either condition are classified as “Standard Systems.”
Clause 2.2 (Base Response Thresholds): Standard Systems require a vendor response within 4 business hours. Critical Systems require a response within 1 business hour.
Clause 2.3 (Escalation Triggers): If downtime exceeds 3 continuous hours, the case automatically escalates to Tier 2 Engineering, regardless of initial classification.
Clause 2.4 (Penalty Calculation): For every full hour or fraction thereof of downtime beyond the contracted 2-hour grace period, the vendor owes a penalty equal to 0.5% of the monthly service fee. Penalties cap at 15% of the monthly fee per quarter.

3. OVERSIGHT ROUTING & COMPLIANCE MATRIX
Automated case routing applies when: (a) historical resolution confidence score exceeds 85%, (b) estimated client exposure is below $50,000, and (c) no regulatory or compliance flags are active. Cases meeting all three criteria proceed to automated resolution queues. If any criterion fails, the oversight system must route the case for Human Review. Note: Compliance_Flag values containing “PII”, “Financial”, or “Cross_Border” trigger an immediate override of automated routing, regardless of confidence scores or exposure values. Sampling protocols apply only to cases flagged for quality assurance audits, not compliance overrides.

4. REPORTING EXCEPTIONS & WAIVER PROTOCOL
General Rule: Any service interruption lasting longer than 4 hours mandates a formal Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report submitted within 5 business days.
Exception 4.1: The RCA requirement is waived if the interruption was caused by an “Automated Failover Routine” AND the Data Loss Metric registers exactly zero records. This exception applies only when both conditions are explicitly logged in the incident summary. If the trigger source is listed as “Manual Intervention,” “Ad-Hoc Patch,” or “Scheduled Maintenance,” the general rule remains in force.

5. PRECEDENCE DIRECTIVES & FINANCIAL SCHEDULES
Rule 5.A: When estimated client financial exposure exceeds $25,000, Penalty Schedule Alpha (immediate invoicing) applies.
Rule 5.B: When an incident occurs during a designated corporate holiday period, Penalty Schedule Beta (deferred quarterly billing) applies.
Precedence Directive: Rule 5.B supersedes Rule 5.A, except in cases formally classified as “Force Majeure,” in which case Rule 5.A remains mandatory. The Force Majeure classification for Case NXF-8842 is currently pending legal review and has not been finalized in this document.

6. REGIONAL ANNEX & OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES
EU-West operations follow Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). Business hours are defined as 08:00–18:00 local time. Response time calculations must convert UTC incident timestamps to local business hours. If an incident begins outside local business hours, the response clock starts at the next local business day opening. All penalty calculations require cross-referencing the downtime duration in Section 1 with the grace period and rate in Clause 2.4. Documentation must be archived in the central compliance repository within 48 hours of case closure.

Signatures:
J. Vance, Service Operations Lead, NexusFlow Analytics
M. Chen, Client Success Director, Aethelgard Logistics
Document Status: Final Draft v1.3 | Audit Reference: NXF-OPS-2024-Q4

definitions.Geo-Fenced Payload: A data batch is strictly classified as a Geo-Fenced Payload ONLY if it simultaneously satisfies both conditions: (1) the HTTP header `geo_origin` is explicitly set to a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, AND (2) the payload is encrypted using AES-256-GCM with a key rotated within the last 48 hours. Mere geographic metadata in the JSON body or standard TLS encryption does not qualify.
definitions.Quarantine Window: The period during which a non-compliant batch is held in isolated storage before automatic deletion or manual override.
definitions.Tier-1 Partner: Any counterparty with a signed SLA exceeding $500k annual volume and a dedicated schema registry account.

clauses.text: All Geo-Fenced Payloads originating from the EU region must undergo a mandatory 72-hour quarantine window prior to downstream processing, unless an expedited waiver is attached.
Retry logic for failed validation steps is capped at three (3) attempts. However, if the payload size exceeds 50MB, the retry cap is reduced to one (1) attempt to prevent resource exhaustion.

Upon exhaustion of the retry cap, the batch must be routed to the quarantine storage. Exception: if the `priority_flag` metadata field is set to `true`, the batch bypasses quarantine and escalates directly to the Senior Data Engineer queue for manual schema reconciliation.
Quarantine windows are calculated in UTC. If the originating system operates on a non-UTC timezone, the hold duration is extended by the absolute value of the timezone offset in hours.

### 3. FOOTNOTES & DEFINITIONS
1. **Accessorial Tiers:** T1 = Liftgate + Inside Delivery; T2 = Liftgate Only; T3 = Terminal Only. Rates exclude fuel surcharge index (FSI), calculated weekly per DOT guidelines.
2. **Route Prefixes:** Routes prefixed with `X-` denote Pre-Cleared Express Lanes. These lanes utilize bonded carrier networks and are exempt from standard delay queues (DEL_Q) and routine customs holds.
3. **Commodity Class Mapping:** Class 50-60 = Standard Dry; Class 65-70 = Climate-Controlled or Palletized; Class 80-85 = Heavy/Oversized Machinery.
4. **Temperature Requirements:** "Ambient" indicates no active refrigeration. "15-25°C" indicates passive insulation acceptable. "≤4°C" indicates active mechanical refrigeration mandatory.
5. **Logger Certification:** Model DL-8 and older units are deprecated for cold-chain compliance. DL-9 and DL-10 are certified. Calibration certificates must be issued within 180 days of the shipment origin date to remain valid.
6. **Delay Queue (DEL_Q):** Status assigned when carrier ETA exceeds contracted window by >12 hours. Triggers automated oversight per Section 4.

### 4. OPERATIONAL RULES & PRECEDENCE MATRIX
**4.1 Oversight Routing Protocol**
When a shipment carries an Oversight Trigger of `INTL/VAL` or `COLD`, the automated system shall evaluate: (a) Declared Value threshold, (b) Route classification, (c) Status code. If `DEL_Q` status combines with Declared Value > $50,000 on an international route, the default action is `HUMAN_REVIEW`. However, routes prefixed with `X-` are pre-cleared express lanes and bypass DEL_Q oversight triggers entirely, routing to `CONTINUE`.

**4.2 Cold-Chain Refund Eligibility Policy**
Refunds for temperature excursions are granted only if all three clauses are satisfied sequentially:
- **Clause A:** Shipment must be classified as "Perishable". For AGL, "Perishable" is strictly defined as goods requiring active mechanical refrigeration maintained at ≤4°C throughout transit. Temperature-sensitive goods, pharmaceuticals, or items using passive insulation do not qualify under this definition.
- **Clause B:** If Clause A is met, the shipment must utilize a certified data logger (Model DL-9 or newer).
- **Clause C:** If Clause B is met, the logger's calibration certificate must be dated within 180 days of the shipment origin date.
Failure at any clause terminates evaluation; no refund is issued.

**4.3 Surcharge & Exemption Precedence**
When multiple financial adjustments apply to a single shipment, conflicts are resolved by strict hierarchical precedence:
1. Master Contract Addendum (Client-specific caps/waivers)
2. Regional Holiday Schedule (Statutory holiday exemptions)
3. Standard Weekend/After-Hours Tariff (Baseline surcharges)
Adjustments are applied top-down. Lower-tier rules are nullified if a higher-tier rule explicitly overrides them.

**4.4 Vendor Incident Report Evaluation Rubric**
Third-party carrier compliance reports are scored against the following ranked criteria for approval:
1. **Root Cause Identification:** Must isolate the single point of failure with supporting data; speculative or multi-factor attributions without primary driver identification are non-compliant.
2. **Corrective Action Timeline:** Must specify measurable milestones with exact dates; vague promises or open-ended commitments are rejected.
3. **Formatting & Tone:** Professional structure, consistent branding, and concise language; minor stylistic flaws are tolerated if criteria 1 and 2 are met.

AEGIS MUTUAL INSURANCE CO. | COMMERCIAL CLAIMS ASSESSMENT DOSSIER
Claim Reference: CM-2024-8891-X
Policy Number: PFF-8842-VEH
Insured: Vanguard Logistics Ltd.
Primary Contact: Marcus Thorne, Fleet Operations Manager
Assigned Adjuster: Elena Rostova, Senior Claims Examiner
Date of Assessment: November 14, 2024

[EXECUTIVE SUMMARY / PRELIMINARY NOTE]
ADJUSTER PRELIMINARY NOTE: Based on initial triage, this claim is approved in full under Section 4.2 (Direct Physical Loss). No deductible will be applied as the incident qualifies for the "Acts of Nature" waiver outlined in the summary box. Proceed to settlement authorization.
Note: This summary is generated by the automated routing system and does not supersede the binding policy language contained in Section 8.1 or the definitions in Appendix A. All approvals remain subject to final manual review.

[INCIDENT & CHRONOLOGY]
On October 28, 2024, at approximately 14:30 local time, a severe convective storm system impacted the Vanguard Logistics depot at Sector 7, Industrial Park. High-velocity winds exceeding 90 km/h caused the partial collapse of the corrugated metal roof structure covering Bay 3. Falling debris and subsequent water intrusion damaged three (3) Class-A refrigeration units and one (1) automated palletizing conveyor. Operations in Bay 3 were halted immediately. Water extraction and temporary tarping were initiated by third-party contractors on October 29. The claim was formally logged into the Aegis portal on November 2, 2024.

[POLICY PROVISIONS EXTRACT]
SECTION 3: COVERAGE TRIGGERS & EXCLUSIONS
3.1 Direct Physical Loss: Coverage applies to tangible damage to insured property caused by a covered peril. Losses must be reported within ten (10) business days of discovery, excluding the day of discovery.
3.2 Consequential Loss Exclusion: The policy does not cover loss of income, lost profits, or increased cost of working, except as expressly provided in the Business Interruption Rider.
3.3 Business Interruption (Defined Term): For the purposes of this policy, "Business Interruption" strictly refers to the forced cessation of core revenue-generating operations for a continuous period exceeding seventy-two (72) hours due to direct physical damage to the primary production facility. It expressly excludes scheduled maintenance, voluntary shutdowns, or partial bay closures where alternative routing remains viable.
3.4 Primary Production Facility (Defined Term): Refers exclusively to enclosed structures designated on Schedule B as "Revenue-Generating Core." Auxiliary storage, parking, and non-billable maintenance bays are excluded from this definition.

SECTION 4: CLAIMS ADJUSTMENT & DEDUCTIBLES
4.1 Standard Deductible: A fixed deductible of $2,500 applies to each covered occurrence.
4.2 Waiver Conditions: The deductible may be waived only if the total validated claim amount exceeds $50,000 AND the peril is classified as a "Category 4 or higher" event per the National Weather Service scale. Storms rated below Category 4 do not qualify for waiver, regardless of wind speed estimates.
4.3 Settlement Basis: Repairs or replacements are settled on an Actual Cash Value (ACV) basis unless the Replacement Cost Endorsement (RCE) was active and properly funded at inception. RCE requires submission of a sworn statement of loss within 60 days.

SECTION 5: VENDOR & REPAIR CONSTRAINTS
5.1 Approved Network: All major equipment replacements must utilize Aegis-approved vendors to maintain RCE eligibility.
5.2 Downtime Limit: Coverage for rental equipment is capped at twenty-one (21) calendar days. The rental period begins on the date of the incident. The twenty-first calendar day is the final day of coverage. Extensions require pre-authorization.
5.3 Mitigation Duty: The insured must take reasonable steps to prevent further damage. Failure to mitigate may result in proportional reduction of the settlement.

SECTION 6: APPRAISAL & DISPUTE RESOLUTION
6.1 If parties cannot agree on ACV, either may demand appraisal. Each party selects an appraiser; appraisers select an umpire. Award is binding if two agree.

[FINANCIAL SUMMARY & SETTLEMENT PARAMETERS]
Total Validated Loss: $48,200
Less Deductible: $2,500 (Waiver eligibility under review)
Net Payout: $45,700
Notification Timeline: Incident discovered Oct 28 (Monday). Portal logged Nov 2 (Saturday). Business days elapsed: Tue(1), Wed(2), Thu(3), Fri(4), Mon(5), Tue(6), Wed(7), Thu(8), Fri(9), Mon(10). The November 2 submission falls on a Saturday, which is excluded from business day counting per Section 3.1.
Tax Note: All settlement figures are quoted pre-tax. The $50,000 waiver threshold in Section 4.2 applies to the gross claim amount before any municipal business tax adjustments.

[EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT ANALYSIS & CONSTRAINTS]
The damaged palletizing conveyor (Asset ID: PC-772) requires full replacement. The insured has requested immediate procurement. Below are the viable options evaluated against policy constraints and operational priorities.
Priority Directive: Minimize total out-of-pocket cost to the insured, subject to hard constraints.
Hard Constraints:
- Must be sourced from an Aegis-approved vendor (per Section 5.1).
- Lead time must not exceed 18 calendar days to avoid triggering the Section 5.2 rental cap breach.
- Unit cost must not exceed the ACV limit of $42,000.
Options:
A) Vendor Alpha: Lead time 20 days. Unit cost $38,000. Status: Unapproved vendor.

**TICKET:** ALS-7842 | **PROJECT:** CargoTrack v4.2 | **TYPE:** Feature/Refactor
**TITLE:** Implement dynamic route-optimization fallback for edge-compute nodes
**AUTHOR:** Juno Vance (jvance@aethelgard.com) | **ASSIGNEE:** Dr. Aris Thorne (athorne@aethelgard.com)
**STATUS:** Code Review Pending | **PRIORITY:** High
**CREATED:** 2024-10-14 09:12 UTC | **UPDATED:** 2024-10-15 14:30 UTC

**DESCRIPTION:**
Current route-optimization logic fails gracefully only when primary cloud endpoints respond within acceptable latency bounds. Under sustained high latency conditions, the system currently retries indefinitely, causing thread pool exhaustion on edge-compute nodes. This PR introduces a deterministic fallback that switches to a pre-computed static routing table when consecutive timeout events occur. The fallback mechanism must activate only after a strict retry limit is reached and must fully respect the Data Handling & Deployment Compliance Framework v3.1 regarding telemetry retention and audit classification. No external dependencies may be introduced.

**ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:**
1. Fallback triggers after exactly three consecutive timeout events (must not trigger on first failure).
2. Static routing table must be loaded exclusively from `/etc/cargotrack/routes_fallback.json`.
3. Telemetry logs for fallback events must be automatically purged after 72 hours to comply with Section 4.2 of the Compliance Framework.
4. CI pipeline must pass all unit, integration, and security scans without critical failures.
5. Zero new external dependencies introduced.

**CODE DIFF:**
```diff
--- a/src/optimization/route_handler.py
+++ b/src/optimization/route_handler.py
@@ -14,11 +14,28 @@
from utils import telemetry_logger
from config import get_latency_threshold

class RouteOptimizer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.cloud_client = CloudClient()
-       self.timeout_count = 0
+       self.timeout_count = 0
+       self.max_retries = 3
+       self.fallback_table = None

    def calculate_route(self, origin, destination):
+       # Check if fallback is already active
+       if self.fallback_table is not None:
+           return self.fallback_table.lookup(origin, destination)
+
        try:
-           return self.cloud_client.query(origin, destination)
+           result = self.cloud_client.query(origin, destination)
+           self.timeout_count = 0 # Reset on success
+           return result
        except LatencyError:
-           raise
+           self.timeout_count += 1
+           if self.timeout_count >= self.max_retries:
+               self._activate_fallback()
+           raise RetryableError("Cloud optimization delayed")
+
+    def _activate_fallback(self):
+       self.fallback_table = StaticRouteTable("/etc/cargotrack/routes_fallback.json")
+       telemetry_logger.log_event("FALLBACK_ACTIVATED", node_id=self._get_node_id())
+       self._schedule_purge(72)
```

--- DESCRIPTION ---
Implement updated access evaluation logic for Service Accounts and High-Risk actions per NexusStream Policy POL-ACCESS-2024-v3. Current implementation blocks all Service Account (SA) access to Production, causing CI/CD pipeline failures. The new policy allows SAs with short-lived tokens but enforces stricter approval workflows for external access to high-risk resources.

Context:
- Actor USR-8842 is assigned Role 'DataAnalyst' in IAM.
- Service Account USR-SVC-99 is used by the deployment bot.
- Emergency Access requests bypass MFA requirements per verbal agreement with CISO during the incident review.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Service Accounts must be allowed if Token Age < 15 minutes.
2. High-Risk Actions from External IPs must require an Approval Token.
3. MFA must be enforced for High-Risk Actions unless exempted by role.
4. Rate limits must be applied based on user tier.

Diff: auth/evaluator.py (Commit 8a4b2c1)

--- POLICY EXTRACT: POL-ACCESS-2024-v3 ---
Effective Date: 2024-05-01
Version: 3.1.0
Owner: Security Governance Board

NOTE: SUMMARY
All access to Production environments requires Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), without exception. Service Accounts must undergo MFA challenges via hardware token binding. Emergency Access grants full bypass of all controls for immediate remediation.

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 'High-Risk Action': Any operation listed in Appendix B, excluding operations performed on environments explicitly designated as 'Sandbox' or 'Dev-Sim'.
1.2 'Privileged User': Any human user with Role Tier 1 or Tier 2. This definition excludes automated service principals and daemon accounts.
1.3 'External IP': Any source address not matching the CIDR ranges in Appendix C.

2. SCOPE
This policy applies to all AuthGate evaluations for Production, Staging, and DR environments.

3. AUTHORITY
3.1 In the event of a conflict between ticket descriptions, review comments, or summary notes and the normative clauses of this policy, the normative clauses prevail.

4. ACCESS CONTROLS
4.1 MFA Requirement: If a request constitutes a 'High-Risk Action', MFA verification is mandatory before authorization.
4.2 Approval Requirement: If a request constitutes a 'High-Risk Action' AND the source is an 'External IP', an Approval Token from a Tier 1 manager is mandatory.
4.3 Service Account Exemptions: Requests originating from a role classified as 'ServiceAccount' are exempt from Clause 4.1 (MFA Requirement) provided the Token Age is less than 15 minutes. Service Accounts remain subject to Clause 4.2 and all rate limits.
4.4 Token Expiry: Service Account tokens must not exceed a lifetime of 15 minutes. Requests presenting tokens older than 15 minutes must be denied immediately.

5. OVERRIDES
5.1 Emergency Access: Requests flagged as 'Emergency Access' bypass Clause 4.2 (Approval Requirement) but retain the obligation to satisfy Clause 4.1 (MFA Requirement) unless the user is a ServiceAccount subject to Clause 4.3.

6. RATE LIMITING
6.1 All requests are subject to rate limits defined by the user's Tier.
6.2 Tier Thresholds:
   - Tier 1: 100 requests/hour.
   - Tier 2: 40 requests/hour.
   - ServiceAccount: 500 requests/hour.
6.3 Requests exceeding the threshold result in a DENY response.

APPENDIX A: ROLE TIER MAPPING
Role 'Admin' -> Tier 1
Role 'DataAnalyst' -> Tier 2
Role 'Viewer' -> Tier 3
Role 'ServiceAccount' -> ServiceAccount

APPENDIX B: HIGH-RISK ACTIONS
- DROP_TABLE
- GRANT_ADMIN
- EXPORT_PII
- DELETE_BACKUP
- MODIFY_WALLET

2.2b If Restricted, multiply current fee by 1.15.
2.2c If both Urgent and Restricted applied, cap fee at Base Fee × 1.30.

**2.3 Carrier Liability**
"NebulaFreight" is Tier B. Tier B max liability is $50,000 per shipment.
Cap lifted only if: Shipment has "High Value" flag AND Cert is "Class A".

**2.4 Service Response Rubric**
Levels: 3 (Best) to 0 (Worst).
L3: Tracking + Logs provided; AND (Delay < 30m OR Waiver Code issued).
L2: Tracking + Logs provided; AND Delay ≥ 30m with valid explanation; AND No data missing.
L1: Tracking OR Logs missing; OR Data incomplete.
L0: No response.

**2.5 Status Authority**
Conflict Rule: Ledger Status governs release. Notes/Footnotes modify status ONLY if tagged "[COMPLIANCE HOLD]".
Footnote ^1: SHP-9924 "Audit Pending" note lacks [COMPLIANCE HOLD] tag.

**2.6 Definitions**
"Temp Variance Report" requires max-min range calculation. "Real-time tracking" requires timestamped node updates. "Valid explanation" requires root cause identification. "Waiver Code" is a 6-digit alphanumeric string issued by Compliance.

3. AUDIT LOG: CLIENT QUERY
Request [Dr. Thorne]: "Verify SHP-9921 integrity. Need real-time tracking history and temp variance report. Confirm delay status."
Response [Ops Team]: "Real-time tracking history exported. Temp variance report attached (Range 0.5°C). Shipment delivered with 45-minute delay vs SLA. Cause: Port congestion. No waiver code issued."

CLAIM REF: AG-8842-VL | DATE: 2024-03-15
CLAIMANT: Vance Logistics Ltd (Policy No. VLG-9901)
ADJUSTER: M. Thorne, Aegis Mutual Commercial Division
SUBJECT: Cargo Damage & Consequential Loss Assessment

INCIDENT SUMMARY: On 2024-03-10, a refrigerated trailer (Unit #RT-442) en route to Port Sterling experienced compressor failure at Mile Marker 112. Digital temperature logs confirm a steady rise to 8°C over a continuous 6-hour window. Claimant reports 4,200 kg of perishable goods (Grade-A produce) were compromised. Vance Logistics requests full cargo replacement ($42,000) plus $15,000 in delayed delivery penalties per their shipping agreement.

POLICY EXCERPTS (VLG-9901):
Clause 4.1 (Covered Peril): Damage resulting from sudden mechanical failure of refrigeration units is covered, provided failure was not due to deferred maintenance. Maintenance logs must be current within 30 days of the incident date.
Clause 4.3 (Temperature Threshold): Coverage for perishables applies only if logs show temperature exceeded 5°C for more than 4 consecutive hours.
Clause 5.2 (Consequential Loss): "Business interruption" explicitly excludes penalties, fines, or liquidated damages imposed by third-party commercial contracts.
Clause 6.1 (Deduction & Subrogation): A 10% deductible applies to cargo claims under $50,000. If salvage value exceeds 20% of the claimed cargo amount, Aegis Mutual reserves subrogation rights over recovered goods.
Clause 8.1 (Salvage Waiver Exception): The subrogation right in Clause 6.1 is waived if the final certified salvage value is under $8,000.
Definition: "Salvage value" refers strictly to the net resale price of damaged goods after certified professional refurbishment, excluding scrap weight estimates or unverified buyer offers.

ADJUSTER NOTES: Maintenance record for RT-442 was last filed on 2024-01-05, which is 69 days prior to the incident. Compressor failure aligns with manufacturer wear patterns. Temperature logs validate the 6-hour breach above 5°C. Third-party penalty contract (Contract #PS-77) specifies $15,000 liquidated damages for delays exceeding 24 hours. Final salvage auction estimate is currently pending. Claim status: Pending final review.

Subject: LEASE RENEWAL & TI REQUEST - MERIDIAN TOWER SUITE 400 (MD-8842)
From: Elias Vance <e.vance@aetherdynamics.com>

Aether Dynamics is preparing to exercise the first renewal option under Lease Agreement MD-8842 for Suite 400, expiring 31 Dec 2025. We intend to submit the signed renewal notice by 15 Dec 2025 to trigger the Early Renewal Discount. Concurrently, we require a Tenant Improvement (TI) allowance to upgrade the eastern server corridor to support next-gen liquid cooling infrastructure. Please confirm the applicable TI rate per the current lease terms, the revised base rent schedule, and any CAM pass-through adjustments for the renewal term. We will forward the architectural schematics once the allowance is confirmed.

Regards,
Elias Vance
Director of Facilities, Aether Dynamics

---

Subject: RE: LEASE RENEWAL & TI REQUEST - MERIDIAN TOWER SUITE 400 (MD-8842)
From: Clara Lin <c.lin@meridianholdings.com>
To: Marcus Thorne <m.thorne@vanguardleasing.com>; Julian Cross <j.cross@vanguardleasing.com>; Elias Vance <e.vance@aetherdynamics.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 14:32:05 UTC

Marcus, please pull the standard TI allowance matrix for Class A commercial suites. Julian, I need your eyes on the renewal discount mechanics before we commit. Elias, thank you for the advance notice. Per Section 12.1, TI requests must be submitted in writing with vendor quotes. Clara

---

Subject: RE: LEASE RENEWAL & TI REQUEST - MERIDIAN TOWER SUITE 400 (MD-8842)
From: Marcus Thorne <m.thorne@vanguardleasing.com>
To: All
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:15:44 UTC

Team,

Per the base lease, the standard TI allowance for renewal tenants is $15.00 per usable square foot. Suite 400 measures 4,200 USF, yielding a maximum draw of $63,000. Base rent for the renewal term (2026-2030) will follow the Standard Annual Escalation (SAE) at 3.5% compounded. However, if the renewal notice arrives after 31 Dec 2025, the Late Signing Surcharge (LSS) of 2.5% applies to Year 1 rent. 

Regarding CAM charges, Annex B classifies Meridian Tower as a "Class A-Prime" asset. Under Section 5.1, Class A-Prime buildings are subject to a Year-Over-Year CAM Pass-Through Cap of 8%. Current 2025 CAM is $0.42/sq ft. If the projected 2026 increase exceeds 8%, the surplus is deferred to a reserve account per Clause 5.3.

Please note Precedence Clause 7.2: "Where the Early Renewal Discount, Late Signing Surcharge, and CAM Pass-Through Cap conflict in application, the Late Signing Surcharge shall override the Early Renewal Discount for base rent calculations, and both shall yield to the CAM Pass-Through Cap for operating expense allocations."

Marcus Thorne
Senior Property Manager, Vanguard Leasing Group

---

Subject: RE: LEASE RENEWAL & TI REQUEST - MERIDIAN TOWER SUITE 400 (MD-8842)
From: Julian Cross <j.cross@vanguardleasing.com>
To: All
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 11:40:19 UTC

Correction on the TI allowance: Amendment 3, executed 14 Mar 2024, revised the renewal TI matrix. The current rate is $12.50 per usable square foot, not $15.00. The $15.00 figure applied to initial occupancy only. Max draw is therefore $52,500.

Additionally, Elias requested an upgrade to the server corridor. Under the lease, this falls under "Qualified Renovations." Note that this defined term is narrower than everyday usage. A "Qualified Renovation" requires: (a) exclusion of any load-bearing or structural modifications, (b) execution solely by Vanguard-approved vendors listed in Appendix D, and (c) submission of a pre-paid commercial general liability certificate naming Meridian Holdings as additional insured prior to material delivery. If any condition fails, the work reverts to standard alterations and triggers full landlord consent fees.

On the CAM calculation: Annex B confirms Class A-Prime. Section 5.1 caps at 8%. 2025 CAM is $0.42. 8% of $0.42 is $0.0336. Therefore, the 2026 CAM cannot exceed $0.4536/sq ft. Any projected increase beyond this triggers the deferral mechanism in Clause 5.3.

Julian Cross
Compliance & Legal Counsel, Vanguard Leasing Group

---

Subject: RE: LEASE RENEWAL & TI REQUEST - MERIDIAN TOWER SUITE 400 (MD-8842)
From: Elias Vance <e.vance@aetherdynamics.com>
To: All
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 16:05:33 UTC

Thank you for the clarifications. Our internal compliance bot generated two draft responses to your terms. Per our internal rubric, please indicate which we should formally execute. The rubric ranks criteria as follows: (1) Strict accuracy of cited lease clauses and defined terms (Highest Weight), (2) Logical sequencing and readability (Medium Weight), (3) Professional tone and formatting (Lowest Weight).

Draft A:
"Aether Dynamics accepts the renewal terms. We acknowledge the $15.00 TI allowance and will proceed with our preferred contractor. We confirm the CAM cap applies and will submit the signed renewal by 15 Dec 2025 to secure the discount."

Draft B:
"Aether Dynamics accepts the renewal. We acknowledge the corrected $12.50 TI allowance per Amendment 3. We confirm the server corridor upgrade meets the "Qualified Renovations" definition by excluding structural work, using a Vanguard-approved vendor, and pre-funding the insurance certificate. We acknowledge Precedence Clause 7.2 and the 8% CAM cap calculation yielding a $0.4536 threshold. Renewal notice will be filed by 15 Dec 2025."

Which draft aligns with your requirements?

Elias

---

Subject: RE: LEASE RENEWAL & TI REQUEST - MERIDIAN TOWER SUITE 400 (MD-8842)
From: Marcus Thorne <m.thorne@vanguardleasing.com>; Clara Lin <c.lin@meridianholdings.com>
To: Elias Vance <e.vance@aetherdynamics.com>

Elias,

Draft B is the only acceptable submission. While Draft A is more polished in tone, it fails the highest-weighted criterion by citing the superseded $15.00 TI rate and omitting the "Qualified Renovations" conditions and Precedence Clause 7.2. Draft B correctly references Amendment 3, explicitly maps the three narrow conditions for Qualified Renovations, and accurately calculates the CAM cap threshold. We will forward Draft B to legal for the final addendum.

Please ensure the vendor quote for the liquid cooling infrastructure is routed through our approved portal by 30 Nov. Once received, we will issue the formal TI draw authorization.

Clara & Marcus

GRIDSYNC REGIONAL TRANSMISSION OPERATOR
INTERCONNECTION AGREEMENT AND TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT REPORT

Case ID: GA-2024-09921
Document Version: 4.1
Date Issued: 2024-11-15

1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION
Applicant: Aethelgard Energy Solutions (AES)
Project Name: Northwood Wind Farm Phase II
Point of Interconnection (POI): Substation N-WD-04, Bus 138kV, Zone 4
Transmission Owner: GridSync Regional Transmission
Regulatory Jurisdiction: Regional Energy Commission (REC) Tariff 2024

2.0 REVISION HISTORY
All revisions listed below refer to the Interconnection Request (IR) submitted by AES. Only the current revision holds validity for technical and financial obligations.

Rev 0 | Date: 2024-02-10 | Status: Initial Filing
Description: Baseline application.
Capacity Requested: 60 MW AC.
Notes: Site survey pending.

Rev 1 | Date: 2024-05-15 | Status: Amended
Description: Expansion of turbine count.
Capacity Requested: 80 MW AC.
Notes: Added 16 turbines. Supersedes Rev 0.

Rev 2 | Date: 2024-08-22 | Status: Superseded
Description: Inverter efficiency upgrade.
Capacity Requested: 85 MW AC.
Notes: Applicant upgraded inverter model to Voltex V-9000, claiming higher yield. Superseded by Rev 3 due to thermal constraints identified in Network Impact Study.

Rev 3 | Date: 2024-10-01 | Status: Current Valid Revision
Description: Capacity derating.
Capacity Requested: 82 MW AC.
Notes: Thermal analysis of Line N-WD-04 indicated overload risk at 85 MW. Applicant agreed to derate nameplate capacity to 82 MW to mitigate ramp stress. This is the approved interconnection capacity for all calculations.

3.0 TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
3.1 Generator Details
Generator IDs: AES-NW-01 through AES-NW-40 (40 units total).
Generator Type: DFIG (Doubly Fed Induction Generator).
Inverter Manufacturer: Voltex Corp.
Inverter Model: V-9000 Series.
Inverter Class: Type-IV Inverter-based Resource (IBR).
Nameplate Capacity per Unit: 2.05 MW.
Total Nameplate: 82.0 MW.

3.2 Control Systems
SCADA Interface: IEC 61850 compliant.
Protection Relays: SEL-751 series at POI.
Communication Latency: < 50ms to GridSync Control Center.

4.0 GRID CODE COMPLIANCE
Compliance is assessed against GridSync Regional Code (GRC-2024).

4.1 Device Requirements (Table T-4)
Table T-4 maps inverter models to mandatory functional requirements.
Entry: Voltex V-9000
- Requirement A: Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) capability per Curve 2.
- Requirement B: Fast Frequency Response (FFR) Enablement.
- Requirement C: Reactive Power capability Q-V curve Class 2.

4.2 Operational Rules
Rule R-FFR-07: "Any generator utilizing an inverter model that mandates FFR Enablement under Table T-4 must demonstrate a ramp rate capability not exceeding 5% of nameplate capacity per second. Exceeding this threshold requires a waiver from the System Operator."

Rule R-VOL-12: "Voltage deviation at the POI must not exceed 2.0% under normal operating conditions. Deviations between 2.0% and 3.5% require installation of a Static Var Generator (SVG) at the applicant's expense."

5.0 NETWORK IMPACT STUDY
5.1 Thermal Analysis
Line N-WD-04 Thermal Rating: 100 MW.
Existing Base Load at POI: 58 MW.
Proposed Injection (Rev 3): 82 MW.
Peak Coincident Load Scenario: 95 MW.
Result: No thermal violation under Rev 3 capacity of 82 MW. Previous Rev 2 (85 MW) resulted in a 103 MW flow, violating thermal limits.

5.2 Voltage Analysis
Voltage profile simulation indicates a maximum deviation of 1.8% at the POI during peak injection. This is within the 2.0% threshold defined in Rule R-VOL-12. No SVG installation is required.

5.3 Curtailment Requirements
Due to congestion on Line N-WD-09 downstream of the tie point, GridSync requires a curtailment schedule.
Curtailment Protocol: During Peak Summer Hours (01-06, 14:00-18:00), injection is capped at 40 MW.
Impact Calculation: Reduction from 82 MW to 40 MW represents a 42 MW curtailment magnitude.
Curtailment Percentage: (42 MW / 82 MW) = 51.2% of nameplate capacity.
Duration Estimate: 360 hours annually based on 5-year weather simulation.

6.0 FINANCIAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE
6.1 Financial Security
Amount Required: $2.5 Million.
Status: Posted.
Date Posted: 2024-03-05.
Instrument: Irrevocable Letter of Credit from First Meridian Bank.

6.2 Environmental and Permits
Environmental Clearance: Granted by REC on 2024-01-15.
Construction Permit: Issued by County Council on 2024-04-10.

6.3 Administrative Notes
Note 6.1: Technical Assessment Report completed and signed off on 2024-07-20 by Lead Engineer M. Kael.
Note 6.2: Applicant submitted Amendment Rev 3 on 2024-10-01.
Note 6.3: All financial obligations are tied to the Current Valid Revision (Rev 3).
Note 6.4: Waiver Directive D-2024-09: "Pursuant to REC policy, any curtailment requirement exceeding 30% of nameplate capacity is waived from mandatory Financial Viability Review (FVR) if the curtailment is restricted to less than 500 hours annually and does not impact base load stability. This waiver applies automatically where conditions are met."

7.0 TIMELINE OF EVENTS
- 2024-01-15: Environmental clearance granted.
- 2024-02-10: Initial Application (Rev 0) filed.
- 2024-03-05: Financial security posted.
- 2024-04-10: Construction permit issued.
- 2024-05-15: Amendment Rev 1 submitted.
- 2024-07-20: Technical Assessment Report finalized.
- 2024-08-22: Amendment Rev 2 submitted.
- 2024-10-01: Amendment Rev 3 submitted; capacity derated.
- 2024-11-15: Agreement issued.

8.0 SIGNATURES
For Aethelgard Energy Solutions:
Name: J. Doe, Project Director
Date: 2024-11-15

For GridSync Regional Transmission:
Name: S. Smith, Senior Interconnection Manager
Date: 2024-11-15

END OF DOCUMENT

Assignee: Marcus Chen | Reporter: Elena Rostova | Status: In Review | Org: Aether Dynamics
Description: Update torque calibration logic per Rev. 3.1. Policy 7.4 states: “For any spec marked REV3.1, the acceptance band is ±5% of the nominal 850 Nm limit. Batches fail if the pass rate falls strictly below 95% or if any reading exceeds the hard ceiling of 870 Nm.”
[CODE]
def validate_torque_batch(readings: list[float], spec_id: str) -> dict:
    if spec_id == "REV3.1":
        limit = 850.0
        tolerance = 0.05
    else:
        limit = 800.0
        tolerance = 0.02
    valid = [r for r in readings if abs(r - limit) <= limit * tolerance]
    pass_rate = len(valid) / len(readings) if readings else 0.0
    critical_fail = any(r > 870.0 for r in readings)
    if critical_fail or pass_rate < 0.95:
        return {"status": "REJECTED", "reason": "Threshold breach"}
    return {"status": "ACCEPTED", "rate": pass_rate}

## 1. GOVERNING RULES & EVALUATION FRAMEWORK
All security incidents logged herein must adhere to the ApexGrid Incident Response Protocol (AIRP v4.2). Initial triage occurs within four (4) business hours of detection. When tabular data conflicts with footnote directives or the governing SLA matrix, the footnote directives hold absolute authority for audit and billing purposes. Vendor mitigation proposals are evaluated using the ApexGrid Risk-Weighted Efficiency Rubric: (1) Constraint Compliance (mandatory), (2) Total Cost of Ownership (lower is better), (3) Implementation Velocity (hours to deployment), (4) Long-Term Resilience Score (1–10 scale). Proposals failing Constraint Compliance are disqualified immediately. Remaining options are ranked strictly by Total Cost of Ownership; ties are broken by Implementation Velocity. Footnote 2: The 'Exempt Flag' in the Rate Matrix indicates whether the lane is eligible for Strategic Partner exemptions. An Exempt Flag of 'N' requires explicit override authorization in the Accessorial Table to waive surcharges. An Exempt Flag of 'Y' automatically suppresses all variable surcharges for that lane.

--- SECTION 2: ACCESSORIAL & SURCHARGE MATRIX ---

| Surcharge Code | Description | Calculation Method | Applicability |
|---|---|---|---|
| FS-24 | Fuel Surcharge | 12% of Base Freight Charge | All Lanes, unless suppressed by Exempt Flag 'Y'. |

| WKD-01 | Weekend Service | $120.00 Flat | Required for deliveries scheduled Saturday/Sunday. |

Footnote 3: Surcharges are cumulative. Where multiple surcharges apply, calculations are performed sequentially: Base Freight → HZ-85 → FS-24 → PS-24. Other accessorial fees are added as flat amounts after variable surcharges.

--- SECTION 3: SERVICE LEVEL & PRECEDENCE RULES ---

| Rule ID | Rule Description | Precedence Hierarchy |
|---|---|---|
| SLA-1 | Standard Transit: 48 Hours. Express Transit: 24 Hours. Clock starts at Origin Scan, ends at Destination Scan. | Base Definition |
| SLA-2 | Weekend deliveries require 'WKD-01' add-on. If 'WKD-01' is not purchased, the SLA clock pauses from Friday 18:00 to Monday 08:00 local time. | Overrides SLA-1 |
| SLA-3 | Late Penalty: Standard 10% refund per 12h late; Express 25% refund per 6h late. Max penalty capped at 50% of line item. | Financial Cap |
| SLA-4 | Safety Override: For Hazardous Materials, late penalties are waived entirely to prioritize safety handling protocols over schedule adherence. | Overrides SLA-3 |
| SLA-5 | Precedence Clause: In the event of conflict, rules are resolved in this order: (1) Safety Overrides, (2) Accessorial Restrictions, (3) Precedence Hierarchy column, (4) General Definitions. | Master Precedence |

--- SECTION 4: OPERATIONAL POLICY & DEFINITIONS ---

Clause 7.1: Delivery Attempts & Business Days.
Delivery attempts must occur within the Service Window. The Service Window is calculated based on 'Business Days'. For the purposes of this agreement, a 'Business Day' excludes: (a) Saturdays and Sundays; (b) Public Holidays in the jurisdiction of the Origin Terminal; (c) Days where the Origin Terminal reports an ambient temperature below -15°C. On non-Business Days, the SLA clock is suspended regardless of service tier.

Clause 7.2: Force Majeure & Extreme Weather.
Carrier liability is suspended for delays caused by Force Majeure events. 'Force Majeure' includes 'Extreme Weather'. 'Extreme Weather' is strictly defined as ambient temperature below -20°C OR precipitation exceeding 100mm in a 24-hour period at the Origin Terminal. Conditions falling below these thresholds do not constitute Force Majeure, even if operations are impacted.

Clause 7.3: Packaging Compliance & Claim Validity.
All shipments must comply with ISTA-3A packaging standards. Carrier reserves the right to inspect packaging upon receipt. If packaging fails ISTA-3A inspection, the shipment is marked 'Rejected'. A 'Rejected' status voids all SLA claims and Late Penalties, and the Shipper is liable for return freight. Packaging inspection results are final and documented in the Claim Adjudication Log.

--- SECTION 5: CLAIM ADJUDICATION RUBRIC ---

When evaluating Late Delivery or Damage claims, Adjudicators must apply the following rubric. The claim outcome is determined by the highest-ranked criterion where the responses differ.

Rank | Criterion | Weight | Evaluation Standard
--- | --- | --- | ---
1 | Packaging Compliance | Critical | Claim must include evidence of ISTA-3A compliance. Failure = Claim Denied regardless of other factors.
2 | Timeliness of Filing | High | Claim must be filed within 48 hours of the event. Late filing reduces payout by 50%.
3 | Evidence Completeness | Medium | Must include BOL, timestamped photos, and weight proof. Missing items result in manual review.
4 | Narrative Clarity | Low | Professional tone and structure aid processing but do not affect eligibility or payout calculation.

--- SECTION 6: SAMPLE CLAIM LOG ENTRIES ---

This framework applies to full-time employees at Level 4 or above. Eligibility for relocation benefits requires minimum 12 months continuous tenure and a current performance status of "Active". Contractors, interns, and employees on administrative leave are excluded.

   - AUTO-APPROVE if: Total Annualized Cost < $80,000 AND Destination is NOT on the Global Sanctions List.

- Beta: DIY assistance. Cost: $8,000. Lead time: 28 days.

- Delta: Rush hybrid. Cost: $11,500. Lead time: 16 days.

AETHELGARD INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY
OFFICE OF GRADUATE ADMISSIONS
INTERNAL PROCESSING MANUAL & CASE LOG EXTRACT
Version 4.2 | Effective: 15 January 2024

1.0 DEFINITIONS AND SCOPE
1.1 “Academic Deficiency” refers strictly to a final-semester undergraduate GPA falling below 2.80, regardless of cumulative GPA or prior academic performance. It does not apply to mid-program transcripts, coursework completed prior to the final academic term, or postgraduate certificates. General academic underperformance outside the final term is classified as “Historical Variance” and follows separate review protocols.
1.2 “Priority Access” status grants applicants early housing selection, waived late-application fees, and guaranteed interview slots. Priority Access is revoked if an applicant requests a deferral beyond 12 months, fails to submit the Verified Financial Attestation Form by the stated deadline, or explicitly selects a pathway that requires its surrender.
1.3 “Credential Packet” denotes the complete set of translated, notarized, and digitally watermarked academic records required for international candidates. A packet is deemed “incomplete” if any single document lacks the official Aethelgard watermark stamp, even if the underlying content is legible, authenticated by the home institution, or accompanied by a cover letter.

2.0 APPLICATION PROCESSING SEQUENCE
2.1 All applications must pass through three sequential validation gates: (A) Document Integrity Check, (B) Academic Threshold Verification, and (C) Financial Eligibility Assessment. Gate B cannot commence until Gate A returns a “Clear” status. Gate C requires the output of Gate B and cannot be initiated concurrently with Gate A.
2.2 Applicants flagged under Clause 1.1 (“Academic Deficiency”) are automatically routed to the Committee on Academic Standing for discretionary review. This review must conclude before Gate C is initiated. The Committee’s determination is final and supersedes standard threshold calculations.
2.3 Late submissions received after 23:59 UTC on the deadline date are subject to a tiered penalty structure. Submissions between 00:00 and 12:00 UTC on the deadline date incur a 50% fee reduction. Submissions after 12:00 UTC incur full penalties. Local time conversions are explicitly excluded from deadline calculations.

3.0 PATHWAY SELECTION & FINANCIAL CONSTRAINTS
Applicants must select one admission pathway upon enrollment confirmation. Selection is irrevocable. Institutional priority for pathway recommendation is to minimize out-of-pocket ancillary fees. Hard constraints for valid selection: (1) Must retain Priority Access status, (2) Must permit off-campus residence, (3) Must not require Exceptional Field Contribution status.
Pathway Alpha: Full tuition coverage. Requires on-campus residence in Building C. Out-of-pocket cost: $4,200/semester. Requires Priority Access status.
Pathway Beta: 75% tuition coverage. Allows off-campus housing or Building D residence. Out-of-pocket cost: $2,100/semester. Does not require Priority Access but does not revoke it.
Pathway Gamma: 50% tuition coverage. Allows any housing arrangement. Out-of-pocket cost: $850/semester. Eligible only if applicant demonstrates Exceptional Field Contribution (defined as 3+ peer-reviewed publications in the target discipline).
Pathway Delta: Standard rate. No coverage. Out-of-pocket cost: $0/semester. Priority Access status is automatically surrendered upon selection. No housing restrictions.

4.0 SUPPLEMENTARY CREDENTIAL PACKET REQUIREMENTS
International applicants requesting transcript evaluation must submit a Credential Packet containing: (i) official university seal on each page, (ii) certified English translation bearing the translator’s license number, (iii) notarization dated within 30 days of submission, and (iv) submission exclusively through the Admissions Portal’s “Secure Upload” module. Email attachments, third-party courier services, portal “Draft” submissions, and uploads to the “My Documents” folder are explicitly excluded from compliance. Non-compliant packets are held in quarantine until correctly resubmitted.

5.0 CASE LOG & CORRESPONDENCE EXTRACT

APPLICANT: Dr. Elias Vance
PROGRAM: MSc Advanced Robotics
DEADLINE: 15 March 2024, 23:59 UTC

LOG ENTRY [2024-03-20 16:30 UTC]: Committee review concluded. Discretionary approval granted. Gate C initiated. Financial Eligibility Assessment pending pathway selection.
LOG ENTRY [2024-03-17 08:40 UTC]: Applicant requested Priority Access verification. System confirmed status active. Note: Priority Access remains valid unless deferral >12 months or Verified Financial Attestation Form missing by deadline.

6.0 ROUTING & ESCALATION PROTOCOLS
6.1 Inquiry Classification Matrix: Requests mentioning “tuition,” “scholarship,” “fee reduction,” or “financial hardship” are frequently misdirected. Per institutional protocol, such inquiries must be evaluated against the substantive nature of the query, not surface terminology.
- If the request concerns eligibility for tuition coverage pathways, housing bundles, or out-of-pocket cost calculations, route to the Admissions Financial Pathways Team.
- If the request concerns visa documentation, SEVIS compliance, international banking authorization, or remittance verification, route to International Student Services (ISS), regardless of financial terminology used.
- If the request concerns transcript evaluation, grade discrepancies, or final-semester GPA calculations, route to the Committee on Academic Standing.
6.2 Surface references to “payment,” “wires,” or “banking” do not automatically trigger ISS routing unless the underlying matter involves immigration compliance or foreign exchange authorization. Misrouted tickets incur a 48-hour processing penalty.

TAGS: [calibration], [hotfix], [series-z9], [line-4]

--- DESCRIPTION ---
The Z-9 linear actuators assigned to Line 4 have exhibited a persistent drift in the final torque application phase over the last 48 production cycles. Metrology data indicates the applied torque is consistently 0.025 Nm below the target, resulting in a rejection rate of 4.2% for end-effector assemblies. Root cause analysis points to thermal expansion in the aluminum housing altering the mechanical preload. The current calibration routine in `calib_z9.py` uses a static offset of 0.02 Nm, which is insufficient for the observed thermal conditions. This change updates the static offset to 0.045 Nm and introduces a dynamic temperature compensation factor based on the housing sensor reading. The compensation factor scales linearly with temperature deviation from the reference 25.0°C.

--- CONTEXT & CONSTRAINTS ---
1. MODEL SPECIFICATIONS:
   - Actuator Model: Z-9 Series.
   - Nominal Torque Spec: 48.0 Nm ± 0.5 Nm (Absolute bounds: 47.5 Nm to 48.5 Nm).
   - Safety Margin Policy: Dynamic adjustments must never exceed 1.15x the nominal spec upper bound (Limit: 55.2 Nm).

--- CODE DIFF (PR #4421) ---
```python
# File: src/controllers/calib_z9.py
# Lines: 14-38

import sys
from sensors import read_housing_temp

# Configuration Constants
REF_TEMP_C = 25.0
TEMP_COEFF = 0.0008  # Compensation per degree Celsius

# Updated static offset based on metrology drift analysis
# Previous value: 0.02
CALIB_OFFSET_NM = 0.045

def apply_torque(target_nm: float, temp_c: float) -> float:
    """
    Calculates the adjusted torque command including thermal compensation.
    
    Args:
        target_nm: The nominal torque target in Nm.
        temp_c: Current housing temperature in Celsius.
        
    Returns:
        Adjusted torque value in Nm.
    """
    # Calculate dynamic compensation factor
    # Factor increases torque slightly as temperature rises to counteract expansion
    delta_temp = temp_c - REF_TEMP_C
    comp_factor = 1.0 + (delta_temp * TEMP_COEFF)
    
    # Apply compensation and static offset
    adjusted = (target_nm * comp_factor) + CALIB_OFFSET_NM
    
    # Safety clamp (enforced by controller firmware, but logged here)
    if adjusted > 55.2:
        sys.warn(f"Torque {adjusted} exceeds safety limit 55.2 Nm")
        
    return adjusted
```

NEXUS-PAY INTERNAL TICKET SYSTEM
================================================
Ticket ID: NEX-4921
Title: [Regression] Tax exemption logic bypasses cert validity and risk scoring for micro-invoices
Status: IN_REVIEW
Assignee: Marcus Wei (m.wei@nexuspay.dev)
Reporter: Sarah Jenkins (s.jenkins@nexuspay.dev)
Priority: High
Labels: invoice-processing, tax-regression, compliance-risk, code-review
Created: 2024-06-14T09:12:00Z
Updated: 2024-06-15T14:30:00Z

--- DESCRIPTION ---
We have identified a regression in the `process_invoice` function following the merge of PR #3310. The new logic incorrectly grants tax exemptions to micro-invoices without verifying vendor risk scores or reseller certificate validity windows. This violates POL-TAX-2024 and exposes NexusPay to audit liabilities.

**Context:**
Invoice INV-2024-8891 was processed with status `exempt` but should have been `taxed`. The vendor, GlobalTrade Inc. (V-992), has an elevated risk profile and an expired certificate. The current code path short-circuits validation for digital goods under $50.

**Requirements for Remediation:**
1. Restore strict validation of vendor risk scores against the De Minimis exemption.
2. Enforce the validity window for Reseller Certificates as defined in policy.
3. Ensure the fix passes the regression test suite, specifically `test_cross_border_micro`.
4. Add an `audit_log` entry for any exemption denial due to risk or certificate failure.
5. **Hard Constraints:**
   - p99 latency increase must be < 5ms per invoice.
   - Validation must be synchronous; eventual consistency is prohibited for tax decisions.
   - **Priority:** Minimize monthly infrastructure cost while satisfying constraints.

--- CODE DIFF ---
File: services/tax_engine/calc.py
Lines: 12-45

```python
@@ -12,10 +12,18 @@ def process_invoice(inv: Invoice) -> Result:
     # Check De Minimis for digital goods
     if inv.amount < 50.0 and inv.type == 'digital':
-        return Result(status='exempt', reason='de_minimis')
+        # FIX: Check vendor risk score before granting exemption
+        risk_score = fetch_vendor_risk(inv.vendor_id)
+        if risk_score > 70:
+            log_audit(inv, 'exemption_denied', 'risk_threshold_exceeded')
+            return Result(status='taxed', reason='risk_voids_de_minimis')
+        return Result(status='exempt', reason='de_minimis')

     # Check Reseller Exemption
     if inv.vendor.has_reseller_cert:
-        return Result(status='reseller_exempt', rate=0.0)
+        # FIX: Validate certificate expiry window
+        if inv.vendor.cert_expiry < (inv.date - timedelta(days=90)):
+            log_audit(inv, 'exemption_denied', 'cert_window_expired')
+            return Result(status='taxed', reason='invalid_reseller_cert')
+        return Result(status='reseller_exempt', rate=0.0)

     # Standard Tax Calculation
     tax = inv.amount * get_rate(inv.vendor.country, inv.category)
     return Result(status='taxed', rate=tax)
```

--- CI/CD OUTPUT ---
Pipeline: nexus-pay-tax-engine #4921
Status: PARTIAL_FAILURE
Duration: 4m 12s

Step: unit_tests
  PASS test_basic_tax_calculation [0.02s]
  PASS test_vendor_risk_fetch [0.01s]
  FAIL test_cross_border_micro [0.08s]
    Assertion Error: Expected status 'taxed', got 'exempt'.
    Input: Invoice(id='INV-2024-8891', amount=45.00, type='digital', vendor_id='V-992', date='2024-06-15')
    Vendor Mock V-992: {country: 'DE', category: 'SaaS', has_reseller_cert: True, cert_expiry: '2023-11-01', risk_score: 72}
    Trace: 
      - De Minimis check triggered (45.00 < 50.00, type='digital').
      - Risk score fetch returned 72.
      - Condition `risk_score > 70` evaluated to True.
      - Audit log written.
      - Result returned `taxed`.
      - WAIT: Post-processor override detected. 
      - Post-processor rule `OPTIMIZATION_CACHE_BYPASS` applied: Vendor V-992 marked as 'trusted_batch' in config cache.
      - Status reverted to `exempt`.

Step: metadata_scan
  WARN: vendor_risk_score=72 detected in test payload metadata.
  INFO: Policy threshold for oversight escalation is 70.
  INFO: Current merge policy requires human review if risk > 70.

Step: integration_tests
  PASS e2e_invoice_flow [12.4s]

--- COMMENTS ---

**Sarah Jenkins** (2024-06-14T10:05:00Z)
Marcus, the diff looks good logically, but the CI failure is strange. The code returns `taxed`, yet the test expects `taxed` and fails? Ah, I see it now. The post-processor is overriding the result because V-992 is in the `trusted_batch` cache. We need to clear that cache or remove the bypass for high-risk vendors. Also, remember the oversight constraint: any ticket touching vendor risk logic where the risk score exceeds 70 must be flagged for human review before merge. The CI metadata scan flagged `vendor_risk_score=72`. Please acknowledge.

**Marcus Wei** (2024-06-14T14:22:00Z)
Thanks, Sarah. I missed the post-processor override. I'll update the config to exclude risk > 70 vendors from the batch bypass.

Regarding the fix strategy, I evaluated three options to implement the cache exclusion and cert validation robustly:

*Strategy A: Synchronous Database Lookup*
- Modify code to query `vendor_risk_db` directly on every invoice.
- Cost: $100/mo (existing DB scaling).
- Latency: Adds 12ms average, p99 adds 14ms.
- Compliance: Full sync validation.

*Strategy B: Redis Cache with TTL and Risk Flag*
- Update Redis cache to include `risk_score` and `cert_valid` flags with 5-minute TTL.
- Cost: $200/mo (Redis cluster expansion).
- Latency: Adds 1ms average, p99 adds 1.5ms.
- Compliance: Sync validation; cache invalidation ensures data freshness within policy limits.

*Strategy C: Async Webhook Validation*
- Send invoice to risk-service via webhook; process tax after callback.
- Cost: $800/mo (New service deployment).
- Latency: 0ms immediate impact (async).
- Compliance: Eventual consistency; tax decision delayed until callback.

I recommend Strategy B. It meets the latency constraint (<5ms), satisfies the synchronous requirement, and minimizes cost compared to C. Strategy A fails the latency constraint.

**Sarah Jenkins** (2024-06-15T09:15:00Z)
Strategy B is approved, but ensure the audit log is present. The ticket requirements explicitly ask for an `audit_log` entry for exemption denials. The diff shows `log_audit` calls, which is good. However, verify that `log_audit` is actually wired to the persistence layer in this branch; the last refactor broke the logger in `calc.py`. If the logger is broken, the deliverable is incomplete.

Also, re-check the oversight decision. The CI output clearly shows `vendor_risk_score=72`. The oversight system policy is strict: risk > 70 triggers a mandatory halt for human review. The ticket cannot be auto-merged. The oversight bot should have flagged this, but it seems it didn't trigger. Please manually escalate this ticket to the Compliance Review Board before merging Strategy B.

**Bot-CI-9000** (2024-06-15T14:30:00Z)

- [ ] Test `test_cross_border_micro` passes. (FAIL)
- [x] Latency constraints evaluated.
- [x] Audit log implementation verified.
- [ ] Oversight escalation completed. (PENDING)

--- POLICY EXTRACT: POL-TAX-2024 ---
**Clause CL-1 (De Minimis Exemption):**
Digital goods invoices with amount < $50.00 are exempt from tax collection.

**Clause CL-2 (Risk Exception):**
The De Minimis exemption under CL-1 is void if the vendor's risk score exceeds 70. In such cases, standard tax rates apply.

**Clause CL-3 (Reseller Exemption):**
Invoices from vendors with a Valid Reseller Certificate are exempt from tax, regardless of amount or type.

**Clause CL-4 (Defined Term: Valid Reseller Certificate):**
A "Valid Reseller Certificate" is defined strictly as a certificate where:
1. The certificate exists in the vendor record.
2. The `cert_expiry` date is greater than or equal to `invoice_date` minus 90 days.
Certificates existing in the record but with `cert_expiry` older than 90 days relative to the invoice date are considered invalid and do not grant exemption.

--- END DOCUMENT ---

TICKET: PR-4892 | VAULTBRIDGE-CORE | CODE REVIEW & DEPLOYMENT GATE
Project: VaultBridge Data Pipeline
Organization: NexusFlow Systems Ltd.
Author: Marcus Thorne (Senior Engineer, Data Platform)
Reviewer: Aria Chen (Staff Engineer, Compliance & Security)
Status: Pending Oversight Decision
Priority: High
Due: 2024-11-15 17:00 UTC

DESCRIPTION:
Implements rate-limiting fallback for the external KYC provider (VeriAuth Inc.) per SLA Annex C, Section 4.2. When VeriAuth latency exceeds 1200ms or returns HTTP 429, the system must route to the secondary provider (ClearID Global) and log the event to the audit trail. The fallback must not be triggered more than 3 times per rolling 15-minute window for a single tenant to prevent cascade failures. Business rule BR-884 requires that fallback requests tagged with risk_level="HIGH" must be held for manual review before processing, unless the tenant holds a Gold-tier contract. This change adds the circuit-breaker logic and updates the routing table.

CODE DIFF (vaultbridge/routers/kyc_router.py):
[Lines 1-48 shown]
def route_kyc_request(tenant_id, payload, risk_level="LOW"):
    primary_provider = "VeriAuth"
    latency_ms = measure_latency(primary_provider)
    
    if latency_ms > 1200 or check_http_status(primary_provider) == 429:
        fallback_count = get_fallback_count(tenant_id, window_minutes=15)
        if fallback_count >= 3:
            raise CircuitBreakerOpen("Fallback limit reached")
        
        if risk_level == "HIGH" and not is_gold_tenant(tenant_id):
            queue_for_review(tenant_id, payload)
            return {"status": "HOLDED", "reason": "HIGH_RISK_MANUAL_REVIEW"}
        
        return route_to("ClearID", payload)
    return route_to(primary_provider, payload)

POLICY & CONTRACT EXTRACTS:
- SLA Annex C, Section 4.2: Primary provider latency threshold is strictly greater than 1200ms. Boundary values are excluded from fallback triggers.
- CAB Directive CAB-2024-088: Deployment windows for core routing modules are restricted to 02:00-04:00 UTC on weekdays. Weekend deployments require VP approval.
- Contract Registry v3.1, Clause 9.1: Gold-tier tenants explicitly waive the manual hold requirement for HIGH_RISK payloads under BR-884. Silver-tier tenants do not qualify for this waiver.
- Audit Policy AP-204: All fallback events must record the exact fallback_count value, the triggering provider, and the tenant contract tier in the immutable audit log.

REVIEW HISTORY:
[2024-11-14 10:15 UTC] Aria Chen: Verified BR-884 alignment. Note: Gold-tier contracts explicitly waive the manual hold for HIGH_RISK payloads per Annex C, Clause 9.1. The 15-minute rolling window is enforced by Redis key expiry. Confirmed TTL matches policy. Audit logging must include the fallback_count value. Added in commit hash a3f9c1. Deploy window restricted to 02:00-04:00 UTC per CAB directive CAB-2024-088.
[2024-11-14 11:02 UTC] Marcus Thorne: Acknowledged. Commit a3f9c1 pushed. Audit logger updated to capture fallback_count, provider_id, and contract_tier. Ready for gate evaluation.

Authorship Override Policy OR-112: If the ticket author is the sole code reviewer for their own module within a 30-day window, the gate must route to human review regardless of other passing criteria. AETHELGARD DYNAMICS | ACCESS GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK & Q3 PROVISIONING REGISTER
Document Control: ID-AGF-2024-Q3 | Version 4.2 | Classification: Internal-Confidential

--- QUICK REFERENCE SUMMARY ---
Per executive directive issued on 15 March 2024, all Tier-3 system access requests require a single department head approval and a standard 48-hour provisioning window. Temporary credentials auto-expire after 90 days unless manually renewed. This summary is provided for rapid onboarding and should be referenced for routine provisioning workflows.

--- SECTION 1: DEFINITIONS & CORE POLICY CLAUSES ---
1.1 Defined Terms
- "Active Session": For the purposes of this framework, an Active Session is strictly defined as a continuous authenticated interaction involving at least three distinct transactional API calls within a rolling 10-minute window. Idle keep-alive pings, background telemetry heartbeats, and UI refresh tokens are explicitly excluded from this definition.
- "Tier-3 System": Production databases, financial ledgers, core authentication directories, and any environment classified as Critical Infrastructure under ISO 27001 Annex A.18.
- "Provisioning Window": The maximum allowable duration between final authorization sign-off and credential activation.

1.2 Access Provisioning & Probationary Controls
- Clause 4.1: Initial provisioning for any Tier-3 System requires dual authorization. Both the requestor's Department Head and a designated Security Officer must provide written sign-off prior to credential generation.
- Clause 4.2: If the requestor has fewer than 180 days of continuous employment at Aethelgard Dynamics, a mandatory 5-day probationary access period applies. During this period, all Active Sessions are logged at the packet level and reviewed daily by the Access Governance Committee.
- Clause 4.3: Probationary access is automatically revoked if the cumulative duration of Active Sessions exceeds 45 minutes within any single calendar day. This threshold is absolute and cannot be overridden by managerial discretion during the probationary window.
- Clause 4.4: Upon revocation under Clause 4.3, the account enters a mandatory 30-day cooling-off period. No re-provisioning requests may be processed until this period elapses, regardless of business urgency.
- Clause 4.5: Temporary credentials (validity <90 days) must adhere to the standard 72-hour provisioning window and require a completed Business Justification Form (BJF-09) attached to the ticket.

1.3 Escalation & Override Protocols
- Clause 5.1: Overrides to Clauses 4.2 through 4.4 require written consent from the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and must be logged in the Exception Register.
- Clause 5.2: All overrides expire automatically after 14 days unless renewed via the quarterly audit cycle.

--- SECTION 2: EVALUATION RUBRIC FOR ACCESS REQUESTS ---
The Access Governance Committee evaluates all non-standard requests using the following weighted rubric. Criteria are ranked by priority; higher-ranked criteria supersede lower-ranked ones in case of conflict.

Rubric Hierarchy:
1. Business Justification Completeness (Highest Priority) - Must explicitly map requested permissions to a funded project code, define data scope, and outline end-date triggers.
2. Role Alignment Precision - Requested permissions must strictly align with the user's official job description and least-privilege matrix. Extraneous access must be justified.
3. Documentation Formatting & Polish (Lowest Priority) - Includes template adherence, typo-free language, proper header/footer usage, and professional presentation.

Case Comparison Reference (Ticket AX-882):
Requestor: M. Chen | System: Analytics Warehouse (Tier-2)

Response B (Submitted by Engineering Dept): Submitted as a plain text attachment with inconsistent spacing and a missing company logo. Justification reads: "Project Code: PHOENIX-7. Requires read/write access to schema 'inventory_logs' to debug ETL pipeline failures. Access needed until pipeline migration completes on 2024-08-15. Aligns with Senior Data Engineer JD section 4.2."

--- SECTION 3: Q3 PROVISIONING LOG & FULFILLMENT RECORDS ---

All provisioning activities are subject to quarterly review by Vertex Solutions (external auditor). The Access Governance Committee reserves the right to retroactively apply policy clauses to requests processed during grace periods. Discrepancies between summary guidance and codified clauses shall always be resolved in favor of the codified clauses. Log retention is set to 7 years. TICKET: LOGI-492
Title: Update Surcharge & Demurrage Engine for EuroTrans Contract v3.1
Assignee: J. Kaur | Reviewer: M. Al-Fayed | Priority: High

DESCRIPTION:
EuroTrans GmbH disputes charges on recent shipments. We must update the calculation engine to align with Contract v3.1. The request includes implementing Perishable surcharges, correcting Heavy weight thresholds, and refining demurrage logic for Priority services.

ATTACHED POLICY EXTRACT (Contract v3.1):
Section 2: Surcharges
2.1 Hazmat Surcharge: +$50.00 per shipment.
2.2 EU Surcharge: +$20.00 per shipment for destinations in the EU.
2.3 Perishable Surcharge: +$30.00. Applies only if `sensor_id` is present and valid in the manifest.
2.4 Heavy Surcharge: +$100.00 if Weight > 1000kg.
2.5 Precedence: If a shipment is flagged as both EU and Hazmat, the EU surcharge supersedes the Hazmat surcharge. In this case, Hazmat=$0.00 and EU=$20.00.

Section 3: Demurrage
3.1 Free Period: 72 hours for Standard service; 48 hours for Priority service.
3.2 Priority Definition: Shipments where `service_level` equals 'EXP'.
3.3 Congestion Multiplier: If cause is 'Port Congestion', apply 1.5x multiplier to demurrage charge.
3.4 Exclusion: The term 'Port Congestion' in Clause 3.3 explicitly excludes delays caused by 'Customs Hold'.

Section 4: Deployment Oversight
4.1 Auto-merge allowed if `risk_score` < 50.
4.2 EU Region Exception: Deployments targeting the `prod-eu` environment require `human_approval=true` regardless of risk score.

CODE DIFF (calc_engine.py):
```python
def calculate_charges(weight, vol, is_haz, is_eu, is_perm, sensor_id, 
                      service_level, det_hours, cause, rate):
    surcharge = 0.0
    # Surcharges
    if is_haz:
        surcharge += 50.0
    if is_eu:
        surcharge += 20.0
    if is_perm:
        surcharge += 30.0
    if weight >= 1000:
        surcharge += 100.0
    
    # Demurrage
    free_period = 48 if service_level == 'EXP' else 72
    billable_hours = max(0, det_hours - free_period)
    demurrage = billable_hours * rate
    
    if cause == 'Port Congestion':
        demurrage *= 1.5
        
    return surcharge, demurrage
```

Job: build-and-deploy
Status: SUCCESS
Risk Score: 42
Region: prod-eu
Hotfix Flag: False
Human Approval: False
Auto-merge: TRIGGERED
Test Suite: All 14 tests passed.

[Dev J. Kaur]: Logic updated per spec. Tests green. Auto-merge should handle this since risk is 42.

DESCRIPTION:
The Fall 2024 admissions cycle requires an update to the eligibility validation service to align with the newly ratified Academic Policy Framework v2.4.1. The current implementation incorrectly applies eligibility flags in a flat, non-hierarchical manner, causing false rejections for partner-institution applicants and legacy candidates. Additionally, the submission endpoint is returning 500 Internal Server Error responses during the final review step, which is blocking manual overrides.

POLICY EXTRACT (Academic Policy Framework v2.4.1):
Section 4.2 - Eligibility Determination:
Rule A (Standard GPA Threshold): Applicants with a cumulative undergraduate GPA below 3.2 are automatically flagged as "Uneligible".
Rule B (Partner Institution Clause): Graduates from the Tri-State Alliance network receive a "Conditional Eligible" status regardless of GPA.
Rule C (Alumni Legacy Provision): Direct descendants of alumni who donated to the capital fund receive a "Priority Eligible" status regardless of GPA.
Precedence Directive: When multiple eligibility flags are triggered for a single application, the system must resolve conflicts using the following hierarchy: Legacy Provision > Partner Institution Clause > Standard GPA Threshold. Lower-priority rules are suppressed if a higher-priority rule activates. No manual override may bypass this hierarchy without Dean-level authorization.

Section 4.5 - Financial Documentation:
General Rule: All applicants requiring institutional financial aid must submit a completed COA (Certificate of Finances) form.
Exception Clause: The COA requirement is waived if the applicant is a citizen of a country with a bilateral tuition reciprocity agreement AND the applicant's designated financial sponsor is a recognized government scholarship body. Both conditions must be verified before waiver approval.

Section 5.1 - Personal Statement Validation Rubric:
Level 0: Fails to parse or contains prohibited content.
Level 1: Major Deficiencies. Word count <600 OR missing ≥2 prompts OR contains ≥3 factual inconsistencies with official transcript.
Level 2: Partial Compliance. Word count 600-749 OR missing exactly 1 prompt OR contains 1-2 factual inconsistencies.
Level 3: Full Compliance. Word count ≥750 AND addresses all 3 prompts AND contains zero factual inconsistencies.
Deduction Caps: Any statement containing ≥3 factual inconsistencies is hard-capped at Level 1 regardless of word count or prompt coverage. Statements missing ≥2 prompts are hard-capped at Level 0.

CODE DIFF (eligibility_engine.py):

     gpa = applicant.get("gpa", 0.0)
